title: GET /api/gameplan and all 4,385 lines of src/roster_intel/ have zero frontend consumers — no page, no component, no Next bridge route references it
claimUnderTest: server.py::get_gameplan docstring: 'Roster intelligence for one team: needs, window, targets, partners... the API surface over src/roster_intel/'. CLAUDE.md documents the module set as live architecture.
observed: The endpoint answers 200 with a 92 KB, high-quality, heavily self-documenting payload (positional profiles with measured deficits, five-state competitive window, two target engines, an 11-partner model, a Pareto package frontier). Nothing in frontend/ calls it. `grep -rn gameplan frontend/ --include=*.js --include=*.jsx` returns exactly ONE hit and it is a comment in frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js:32. There is no frontend/app/api/gameplan bridge route (the dir listing of frontend/app/api has 18 entries, none named gameplan). Every number this subsystem produces — replacement-relative positional deficit, fragility, tradeable surplus, competitive window, target ranking, partner fit, trade packages — is unreachable by any user.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan?team=468418790212759552' | head -c 200 ; grep -rn 'gameplan' frontend/app frontend/components frontend/lib --include=*.js --include=*.jsx
reproduction.actual: endpoint 200 / 92,044 bytes; grep over frontend source returns 1 hit, a comment in frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js

numericProof.formula: count of frontend fetch/axios call sites targeting /api/gameplan

userImpact: The only lineup-aware, replacement-benchmarked roster analysis in the codebase is invisible. The user's roster judgement comes instead from /rosters (raw value sums) and /phases (a 2x2 median split) — the two crudest of the four team-direction implementations in the tree.

priorFinding.note: Prior area 3 covered /rosters, /phases and terminal but did not test /api/gameplan reachability.

whatWorks: The endpoint itself is correct, fast (405 ms cold team build, 28 ms warm, cache stamped in `timing`), league-scoped, and unusually honest: `coverage`, `fieldPolicy`, `limitations.canSupport/cannotSupport` and per-field `_semantics` are all emitted and accurate.
rootCause: The backend subsystem shipped without a UI; no consumer was ever written.
requiredRepair: Either build the /gameplan (or /rosters) surface that consumes it, or mark the module set explicitly as internal-only so it is not mistaken for live product.
dependencies: W20-F010 (its market/consensus/pick rollups are 0.0), W20-F005 (its window classifier is one of four)

title: On the live /league Trade Deadline board the strongest roster in the league (Brent, ROS strength percentile 100%) is labelled 'Seller — sell aging win-now players' because an owner missing from the playoff sim is scored as 0% playoff odds
claimUnderTest: src/ros/trade_deadline.py docstring: 'Returns one row per team with the direction label + recommendation'; build_team_directions docstring: 'When a map is empty (e.g. no cached sim yet), the missing dimension defaults to 0 — the classifier degrades cleanly.'
observed: data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json contains 8 of 12 owners. Brent, Kich, Blaine and jstuedle are absent. `po = float((playoffs.get(owner) or {}).get('playoffOdds') or 0.0)` turns 'not simulated' into a hard 0.0, indistinguishable from a simulated 0%. Brent is rank 1 of 12 in data/ros/team_strength/latest.json (percentile 1.0) and is classified 'Seller' with recommendation 'Sell aging win-now players. Prioritize 2026/2027 picks and 23-or-younger upside.' The live page renders STRENGTH 100.0% in the column immediately left of the word Seller, with no coverage caveat anywhere on the page.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/rosTradeDeadline' | python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(t['displayName'],t['label'],t['playoffOdds'],t['rosStrengthPercentile'],t['rank']) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['teams']]" ; python3 -c "import json; print([r['displayName'] for r in json.load(open('data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json'))['playoffOdds']])"
reproduction.expected: Brent (rosStrengthPercentile 1.0, rank 1) is not told to sell, or the row is suppressed / flagged as not simulated
reproduction.actual: Brent playoffOdds 0.0, championshipOdds 0.0, rosStrengthPercentile 1.0, rank 1.0, label 'Seller'; sim owner list = [Joey, Jason, Roy, Ty, Eric, MaKayla, Ed, Collin] — Brent absent

numericProof.formula: strength_pct = (total - rank + 1)/total = (12 - 1 + 1)/12 = 1.0 ; label = Seller iff playoff<0.25 and champ<0.02 ; playoff = float(None or 0.0) = 0.0

userImpact: On /league?tab=rosTradeDeadline a manager reads 'Brent — Seller — sell aging win-now players, prioritize picks' next to 'STRENGTH 100.0%'. Four of twelve managers (Brent, Kich, Blaine, jstuedle) get a direction derived from a fabricated 0% rather than a measurement; the top-ranked roster is the worst-affected. Acting on it means selling the league's best team's win-now assets for picks.

priorFinding.note: Prior F04 documented the dead inputs and the unreachable label but not the missing-owner-to-0.0 coercion, which is what produces the wrong ACTION on the strongest roster. Confirmed independently and extended.

whatWorks: src/api/gameplan.py DOES handle this correctly on the same data: it stamps oddsSource='owner_not_in_simulation', leaves playoffOdds/championshipOdds null, and emits a note that the two competitiveness scales are not comparable.
rootCause: `or 0.0` collapses absence into a measurement, and build_section() supplies no coverage information the UI could render.
requiredRepair: Return None for owners absent from the sim, render them as 'not simulated' rather than as a direction, and surface simulation coverage (8/12) on the page.
dependencies: Depends on the ROS playoff-sim workstream for why only 8 owners are simulated.

title: Terminal roster strength is the raw sum of rankDerivedValue over rostered players — no lineup solve, no starter/depth weighting, no positional deficit, and draft picks excluded entirely
claimUnderTest: The terminal header renders 'TEAM VALUE' as the headline roster metric; _rollup_values in the sibling roster_intel engine explicitly warns 'these are portfolio totals, deliberately NOT a strength signal'.
observed: teamAggregates.totalValue == sum(rankDerivedValue) over the roster's player names, exactly, for every team. It ignores the league's 21 starter slots (which the SAME contract ships as sleeper.rosterPositions), ignores positional replacement level, and by design excludes all 216 draft picks in the league. A team with 28 IDP bench bodies and no startable RB scores identically to one with the same total concentrated in starters.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o /tmp/c.json; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal?team=468418790212759552' -o /tmp/t.json; python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('/tmp/c.json')); t=json.load(open('/tmp/t.json')); tm=[x for x in c['sleeper']['teams'] if x['name']=='Jason'][0]; s=sum(int(c['players'][n].get('rankDerivedValue') or 0) for n in tm['players']); print('recomputed',s,'terminal',t['teamAggregates']['totalValue'],'picksHeld',len(tm['picks']),'byPosition.PICK',t['portfolio']['byPosition']['PICK'])"
reproduction.expected: a lineup-aware or at least starter-weighted strength number

numericProof.formula: totalValue = sum(rankDerivedValue[p] for p in team.players)

userImpact: The home page's headline 'TEAM VALUE' rewards roster hoarding and cannot show a lineup deficit. Jason's 62 picks (worth 158,693 on the same board, 48% of his true asset base) contribute zero, so the terminal's cross-team ordering differs from /rosters' default ordering for the same 12 teams.

priorFinding.note: Prior area 3 findings covered terminal insight cards, not the totalValue definition.

whatWorks: src/api/terminal.py:1206-1231 documents the pick exclusion honestly, including the measured 22.5% league-wide magnitude, and refuses to change it silently. The starter/bench split IS computed — but only in the client fallback (portfolio-insights.js), never server-side.
rootCause: Terminal aggregates were specified as a portfolio total and are presented as a strength signal.
requiredRepair: Either rename the surface to 'portfolio value' or add the lineup solve the contract already carries the slots for (frontend/lib/starter-slots.js::fillLineup already does exactly this on the same data).

title: PortfolioSummary renders a Total Value that excludes picks beside a 'Picks' legend that includes them — the three legend numbers sum to 314,562 under a Total Value of 171,495
claimUnderTest: PortfolioSummary.jsx:149-153 — 'Picks aren't eligible for start/bench slots... Picks still appear in Total Value above and in the PICK column of the positional stack below.'
observed: The merge at :94-106 takes totalValue and byPosition from the SERVER (which excludes picks) and leaves starterValue / benchValue / pickValue / pickCount on the LOCAL object (which includes them). For Jason the panel therefore renders Total Value 171,495 with a legend reading Starters 97,497 / Bench 73,998 / Picks 143,067 — the legend sums to 314,562, 1.83x the stated total. The PICK row of the positional stack is skipped entirely because the server reports count 0, so the comment's second claim is also false.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W20 && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o contract.json && mkdir -p w20 && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal?team=468418790212759552' -o w20/term-468418790212759552.json && node pf.mjs   # see README.md
reproduction.actual: Total Value 171,495 ; Starters 97,497 + Bench 73,998 + Picks 143,067 = 314,562 ; byPosition.PICK = {count:0,value:0,pct:0}

userImpact: On the signed-in home page the portfolio panel is internally inconsistent by 143,067 (83% of the number it displays as the total). A manager comparing their Total Value to another team's cannot tell whether picks are in it.

priorFinding.note: Prior area 3 flagged the buy-low filter and the age curves, not the server/local merge asymmetry.

whatWorks: Both halves are individually correct; only the merge mixes them.
rootCause: src/api/terminal.py deliberately excludes picks (documented) while frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js deliberately includes them (documented), and PortfolioSummary merges field-by-field without reconciling the asset scope.
requiredRepair: Pick one scope. If the server stays pick-free, drop the local pickValue legend and the byPosition.PICK row; if picks belong in the total, inject them server-side.

title: frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js prices every current-year draft pick at zero — 15,626 per team, 187,512 league-wide (39% of all pick capital) — because it is the one pick join in the tree that ignores contract.pickAliases
claimUnderTest: portfolio-insights.js:239-258 — 'With it, 216 of 288 resolve. The other 72 are RIGHT to be unresolved: they are every 2029 pick.'
observed: The join uses resolveByCandidates(byName, buildPickLookupCandidates(name)), which resolves 'YYYY Nth' to the generic row 'YYYY Mid Nth'. For 2027 and 2028 those rows carry a real rankDerivedValue. For the CURRENT year they carry rankDerivedValue = null — the current-year board is priced on the slot rows ('2026 Pick 1.06'), and the contract ships pickAliases specifically to redirect the generic label onto the slot row. trade-logic.js already exports resolvePickRow(label, lookup, pickAliases) which does this and which league-analysis.js uses; portfolio-insights.js never imports it. Result: all six of every team's 2026 picks price at 0. The shortfall is identically 15,626 for all 12 teams. Two teams (Brent, Ed) end with pickValue 0 exactly, so the 'Picks' legend never draws at all.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W20 && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o contract.json && node pickall.mjs   # see README.md
reproduction.actual: A=294,288 vs B=481,800 league-wide; per-team delta is exactly 15,626 for all 12

numericProof.formula: perTeamShortfall = sum(2026 slot values) = 4987+3059+2293+1908+1768+1611 ; leagueShortfall = 12 * perTeamShortfall

userImpact: Anywhere the client-side portfolio path renders (anonymous visitors, pre-fetch paint, terminal error) a team's draft capital is understated by its entire current class. Two of twelve teams show no draft capital at all.

priorFinding.note: The in-file comment shows the pick join was fixed once for the format problem; the aliasing problem was not addressed and the '72 are 2029 picks' explanation does not hold on this snapshot (no team holds a 2029 pick).

whatWorks: league-analysis.js's resolvePickRow path is correct and is what /rosters uses.
rootCause: Two independent pick joins; only one consumes the backend alias map the contract publishes for exactly this purpose.
requiredRepair: Replace resolveByCandidates(...) in portfolio-insights.js with resolvePickRow(name, rowLookup, rawData?.pickAliases) — the import is already in the same module.

title: Four independent team-direction classifiers ship simultaneously and disagree on 9 of 12 teams; three are reachable by a user and none references the others
claimUnderTest: The prior audit says three team-phase classifiers exist. CLAUDE.md describes the five-state competitive window as the roster-intel answer without noting the other three.
observed: There are FOUR. (1) team-phase.js — Win-now/Contender/Mixed/Rebuild, 2x2 median split on top-25 value x median age, rendered on /phases. (2) league-analysis.js::scoreTeamTiers — Contender/Mid-Tier/Rebuilder, score = starters*0.7 + depth*0.2 - picks*0.1, forced thirds (4/4/4), rendered on /rosters. (3) roster_intel/window.py — five affinity-weighted states over (competitiveness, trajectory), served by /api/gameplan, NO UI. (4) ros/direction.py — seven Buyer/Seller labels off playoff+championship odds, rendered on /league?tab=rosTradeDeadline. Run on the same 12 live rosters they agree on only 3 (Jason, Eric, Joey). Brent is simultaneously 'Contender' (1), '#1 Contender' (2), 'championship_contender' at 0.66 confidence (3) and 'Seller' (4). Collin is 'Win-now' (1), '#6 Mid-Tier' (2), 'productive_struggle' (3) and 'Seller' (4). Kich is 'Mixed' (1), '#9 Rebuilder' (2), 'playoff_contender' (3) and 'Seller' (4).

reproduction.expected: one classifier, or explicit reconciliation between them
reproduction.actual: four classifiers; full agreement on 3 of 12 teams; direct contradiction (contender vs seller) on Brent and Collin

numericProof.formula: count of teams whose four labels map to a consistent point on the contend-rebuild axis

userImpact: A manager who opens /rosters, /phases and /league in one session gets three different answers to 'am I contending'. The /rosters page alone shows two of them (see W20-F007).

priorFinding.note: Prior audit named three; scoreTeamTiers is a fourth and is the one shown on /rosters.

whatWorks: window.py is the only one of the four that (a) reports uncertainty, (b) renames its output 'affinities' rather than claiming probability, (c) publishes an ordering caveat, and (d) exposes a manual-override hook. It is also the only one with no user surface.
rootCause: Four surfaces each grew their own direction model; no shared definition module.
requiredRepair: Nominate one classifier (window.py is the best of the four) and make the other three read it or be removed.

title: /rosters shows two contradictory rankings of the same 12 teams on one screen: Jason is #1 in the power table and #5 'Mid-Tier' in the tier cards 400px below
claimUnderTest: /rosters is titled 'Team Strength — Power rankings, position breakdowns, waiver wire, and trade targets.' — a single power ranking.
observed: The page renders buildAllTeamSummaries (sorted by total asset value under the selected scope, default 'Players + Picks') AND scoreTeamTiers (sorted by starters*0.7 + depth*0.2 - picks*0.1, bucketed into forced thirds). On the live snapshot the two orders differ for 10 of 12 teams. Jason: #1 at 328,504 in the table, #5 'Mid-Tier' in the cards. Roy: #7 by total, #11 'Rebuilder'. MaKayla: #3 by total, #4 'Contender'. The divergence is driven entirely by the -0.1 pick term: Jason's 158,400 of pick capital costs him 15,840 score points, which is exactly what drops him from 2nd to 5th.
userImpact: A manager reads '#1' at the top of the page and '#5 Mid-Tier' halfway down, for their own team, with no explanation that the two use different formulas. The tier cards additionally force exactly 4 contenders / 4 mid / 4 rebuilders regardless of how the league is actually distributed.

priorFinding.note: Prior F00 claimed the pick term's NET sign is +0.1 because depthValue carried pick value. At HEAD e96c06ef league-analysis.js:1128 reads `const depthValue = totalValue - starterValue - pickValue;` so the net coefficient is -0.1 as documented. Verified numerically: Jason's score reproduces to 66,760.3 only with the -0.1 net. The sign bug is fixed; the two-rankings-on-one-page problem it sat inside is not.

whatWorks: scoreTeamTiers' starter solve uses the league's real 21-slot lineup via fillLineup and is genuinely lineup-aware; the 'Starters only' scope on the table is too.
rootCause: Two team-ordering functions with different objectives rendered on one page without labelling either.
requiredRepair: Label each block with the formula it uses, or drive both from one score.

title: /phases classifies zero teams as 'Rebuild' on live data, so its headline trade-partner feature renders nothing and the page never says why
claimUnderTest: /phases subtitle: 'Each team classified by top-25 roster value x median age, with natural trade-partner suggestions for your franchise.'
observed: Rebuild requires medianAge STRICTLY below the league median of team medians. Team medians are computed over the top 25 players by value and land on integers; on this snapshot the league median is 26.0 and six teams sit at exactly 26.0, all forced to the 'older' side. Distribution: Win-now 5, Contender 1, Mixed 6, Rebuild 0. partnerships is built as winners x rebuilders, so it is []. The live page renders the 12-row table and then nothing — no partner block, no empty state, no explanation.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W20 && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o contract.json && node tp.mjs   # see README.md
reproduction.expected: at least one Rebuild team and a non-empty partnerships list
reproduction.actual: {leagueMedians:{value:91596,age:26}} ; phases Win-now 5 / Contender 1 / Mixed 6 / Rebuild 0 ; partnerships []

userImpact: The page's stated reason for existing produces no output on the real league and gives the user no signal that anything is missing. Additionally the label set is semantically inverted: the team most in need of a reset (low value, OLD) is labelled 'Mixed' while 'Rebuild' is reserved for low value + YOUNG.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced independently on the live 2026-08-04 contract via the real rankDerivedValue rather than the prior audit's _finalAdjusted proxy. Prior audit measured league median age 25.0 with 5 teams tied and phases 2/4/6/0; I measure 26.0 with 6 tied and 5/1/6/0. Different numbers, identical failure: Rebuild = 0, partnerships = [].

whatWorks: The 2x2 classification itself responds to both axes (see W20-F009); the failure is the strict tie rule plus the top-25 age sample.
rootCause: Strict `<` against a median of integer-valued medians, on a sample (top 25 by value) that systematically excludes the young cheap prospects a rebuild is made of.
requiredRepair: Use a tolerance band or a percentile split, sample age over the whole roster, and render an explicit empty state when partnerships is [].

title: team-phase.js is a pure median split, so a 10x increase in one team's roster value changes nothing while a 50% cut to that team relabels a DIFFERENT team
claimUnderTest: Prompt question: is team direction reducible to average age? Test by perturbing age vs perturbing value.
observed: Perturbation test on the live contract, mutating only Collin's roster: ages -4y -> no change; ages +4y -> Collin Win-now -> Contender; value +50% -> no change; value x10 -> NO CHANGE (Collin is already above the value median, and only the side of the median matters); value -50% -> Collin Win-now -> Rebuild AND Ed Mixed -> Contender, even though Ed's roster was not touched. So the classifier is NOT reducible to age — both axes move it — but it is scale-blind above/below the median and non-local: one manager's trade can relabel a manager who did nothing.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W20 && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' -o contract.json && node perturb.mjs   # see README.md
reproduction.expected: monotone response to value magnitude; a team's label depends only on its own roster
reproduction.actual: value x10 -> no label change anywhere; value -50% -> Collin:Win-now->Rebuild, Ed:Mixed->Contender

numericProof.formula: isHighValue = teamTotal > median(all team totals); the median itself moves when any team moves

userImpact: Half the league is always 'high value' and half always 'low value' by construction, so the page cannot report a league where 9 teams are genuinely strong. And a manager can see their own phase flip because someone else traded.

priorFinding.note: Prior F02 covered the age-tie half of the median problem; the value half and the non-locality are new.

whatWorks: Both axes are live — the classifier is not an age proxy.
rootCause: Both axes are median splits rather than calibrated scales.
requiredRepair: Score against absolute or league-history-calibrated thresholds, not the current league's own median.

title: /api/gameplan reports roster market / consensus / leagueAdjusted / pickValue as 0.0 for all 12 teams while the same payload reports marketPriceCoverage 627 of 666 priced
claimUnderTest: RosterValues docstring: 'Kept as separate fields rather than one blended number: the whole point of the LI-4 schema is that market, consensus and league-adjusted can disagree.' The payload's own fieldPolicy.nullIsNotZero states 'null means the quantity was not measured. It is never collapsed to 0.'
observed: build_league_bundle calls analyze_roster(...) with replacement, player_meta, playoff_odds and lineup_scores but WITHOUT player_values and WITHOUT pick_value, even though _index_contract_players already builds the site-value map (`sites`) two frames up and hands it to the package generator. _rollup_values therefore sums an empty mapping and RosterValues defaults 0.0 survive. All four fields are 0.0 for all 12 teams. Worse, pricedPlayers=57/unpricedPlayers=0 sits next to market=0.0 — pricedPlayers counts ROS pricing, so the payload reads as '57 players priced, market value 0'. The LI-4 separation is real in the schema and collapsed to ROS-only in practice.

reproduction.expected: market > 0 for every team (the contract prices 627 of 666 rostered players)
reproduction.actual: market=0.0 consensus=0.0 leagueAdjusted=0.0 pickValue=0.0 for all 12; only ros/startersRos/benchRos populated

userImpact: Zero today (no UI). If the surface is built as-is, every roster shows a market value of zero next to a coverage line claiming 94% priced.
whatWorks: startersRos / benchRos ARE populated and are a genuine lineup-aware split (Jason 670.76 starters / 530.69 bench). The window, profiles, needs and target engines all run off ros correctly.
rootCause: analyze_roster's optional value arguments are never supplied by the API assembler.
requiredRepair: Pass `sites` (already built at gameplan.py:410) as player_values and the roster's pick total as pick_value, or emit these four fields as null so nullIsNotZero holds.

title: /api/gameplan flags 'only 2 of 3 dedicated DL slots filled' and urgentNeed=true on rosters whose own lineup solve in the same payload reports 21 of 21 slots filled — 6 position rows across 5 of 12 teams
claimUnderTest: needReasons: 'only {entered} of {req} dedicated {pos} slots filled' — presented as a measured lineup gap and used to set urgentNeed.
observed: The test is `pm.entered_lineup < required[pos]`, where entered_lineup counts players whose BASE position is pos that entered ANY slot, and required[pos] counts dedicated slots for pos. In an IDP league with multi-eligible defenders a hybrid classified under LB can fill a DL slot, so the two quantities differ without any slot being empty. Verified: sum(enteredLineup) == filledSlots == 21 == totalSlots for 11 of 12 teams, yet Jason DL reports 2 of 3, Joey DL 2 of 3, Kich DL 2 of 3, Roy DL 2 of 3, Ty LB 2 of 3. Jason's LB row correspondingly reports enteredLineup 4 against requiredSlots 3. Four of the six rows simultaneously report a non-zero tradeableSurplus at the very position they call an urgent need (Jason DL: urgentNeed true AND tradeableSurplus 31.49 with 2 named surplus players). Only MaKayla's K row (0 rostered, 20/21 filled) is a real gap.

reproduction.command: for id in 468418790212759552 1012114412049731584 1208452010173538304 472206636534984704 473973924808355840; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan?team=$id" | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);r=d['roster'];print(d['team']['teamName'],'filled',r['filledSlots'],'/',r['totalSlots'],[(p,x['enteredLineup'],x['requiredSlots'],x['needReasons']) for p,x in r['positions'].items() if x['requiredSlots'] and x['enteredLineup']<x['requiredSlots']])"; done
reproduction.expected: no unfilled-slot reason on a roster reporting filledSlots == totalSlots
reproduction.actual: 5 teams report 'only 2 of 3 dedicated DL/LB slots filled' with filledSlots 21 / totalSlots 21

numericProof.formula: sum over positions of enteredLineup should equal filledSlots; a per-position shortfall is only real if the SUM is short

userImpact: Zero today (no UI). If surfaced, the engine would tell a manager with 7 rostered DL and a full lineup that DL is an urgent hole — at the same time as offering two of those DL as tradeable surplus.
whatWorks: The deficit metric itself is sound and correctly benchmarked: needs[pos].replacementBaseline == replacementLevel * requiredSlots, and deficit = baseline - actualContribution (Jason DL 42.255 - 39.67 = 2.585, exact). The replacement level is league-endogenous (measure_endogenous_starters over all 12 rosters), which is the defensible benchmark. profiles.py also documents at length why fragility must NOT be multiplied by marginal.
rootCause: A base-position entry count is compared against a dedicated-slot count in a league where slot eligibility is multi-position.
requiredRepair: Derive the reason from the solver's actual per-slot assignment (solve_summary already returns it) rather than from grouped entry counts.

title: Of the concentration and depth axes the roster-intel docs describe, positional fragility and tradeable surplus are live; bye-week concentration is null in 104 of 104 position rows, the roster-clogger signal is computed but never emitted, and the elite tier is unreachable
claimUnderTest: profiles.py:6 — 'The descriptive fields (age, injury, bye, tier counts) are exactly...'; marginal.py:156-158 — 'Players with real value that never enter, even though they are rostered — the clog signal.'
observed: Live audit of all 104 position rows across 12 teams. LIVE: fragility (0.109-1.0, real spread), worstAbsenceDrop, tradeableSurplus + named surplusPlayers, meanAge, ageOver28, injuredCount (16 rows at 1, 3 at 2, 1 at 3), injuredStarters, marginalStrengthIndex, marginalShare, entryRate. DEAD: byeConcentration is null in 104/104 because gameplan.py::_index_contract_players builds player_meta with 'age' only and never a 'byeWeek' key, so _bye_concentration always sees zeros. NOT EMITTED: PositionMarginal.cloggerValue and nonEnteringPriced are computed in marginal.py and serialized by its own to_dict, but PositionProfile does not carry them and the gameplan payload contains neither string. UNREACHABLE: tierCounts.elite is 0 in 104/104 because engine.py calls build_position_profiles without league_position_values, so elite_threshold(()) returns None (documented as intentional honest degradation, but the bundle already holds all 12 rosters). ABSENT ENTIRELY: no top-asset concentration (HHI or top-1 share), no NFL-team concentration, no age-concentration metric — grep for hhi/Herfindahl/teamConcentration/topAssetConcentration over src/ and frontend/lib returns nothing.

userImpact: Zero today (no UI). The gap matters for the prompt's question: of the five concentration axes asked about, only positional concentration is real; bye-week is scaffolded-and-starved, top-asset / NFL-team / age concentration do not exist, and productive-depth-vs-clogger exists in code but reaches nothing.

rootCause: player_meta is built with one key; two computed fields are not plumbed into the response dataclass; league_position_values is never threaded from the bundle that holds it.

title: The manual contender/rebuilder override exists only as a function parameter with no caller outside tests — no endpoint, no query param, no user_kv key, no UI
claimUnderTest: window.py:323-330 — 'override_state is the manual hook. It pins the distribution to that state... a manager who says I am rebuilding is stating intent the model cannot observe.'
observed: compute_window and analyze_roster both accept override_state / override_reason and implement them correctly (probability mass 1.0 on the chosen state, overridden=True stamped, model inputs retained for audit). build_league_bundle calls analyze_roster without them. /api/gameplan parses only leagueKey, team/ownerId and partner. Grep over src/, frontend/ and server.py for override_state / overrideState / competitiveOverride / windowOverride returns hits in window.py, engine.py and tests/ only. /settings exposes no contender/rebuilder control. So no manual override can be set, and none of the other three classifiers (team-phase.js, scoreTeamTiers, ros/direction.py) accepts one at all.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'override_state\|overrideState\|competitiveOverride' src/ frontend/ server.py --include=*.py --include=*.js --include=*.jsx | grep -v node_modules ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan?team=468418790212759552&override_state=rebuild' | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['roster']['competitiveWindow']['overridden'])"
reproduction.expected: overridden true when an override is requested
reproduction.actual: grep hits are confined to src/roster_intel/window.py, src/roster_intel/engine.py and tests/; the query param is ignored — measured: overridden False, mostLikely playoff_contender

numericProof.formula: count of non-test call sites passing override_state

userImpact: A manager cannot tell the system 'I am rebuilding'. Every downstream recommendation (target-position win-now weights, partner window alignment, package plausibility) is therefore driven by a model read the user cannot correct.
whatWorks: The override semantics are the right ones — pin rather than blend, and stamp the fact — and the win-now weights it would drive (championship_contender 1.0 ... rebuild 0.15) are already wired into targets.py and declared as unmeasured priors in limitations.keyAssumptions.
rootCause: The hook was written ahead of the surface that would set it.
requiredRepair: Accept an override on /api/gameplan (and persist it per user+league in user_kv) once a UI exists.

title: The terminal labels all 665 rostered players 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers' while the same payload's delta panel correctly says 'Insufficient rank history'; data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist and source_value_history.jsonl holds one day
claimUnderTest: Terminal signals are described as 'Rule-driven Buy / Sell / Hold per roster player'.
observed: data/rank_history.jsonl is absent (the path src/api/rank_history.py:74 resolves to) and data/source_value_history.jsonl contains exactly one date (2026-08-04). Every trend7/trend30/volatility is therefore null and volLabel 'unknown'. All 10 signal rules gate on one of those, so none can fire: 665 of 665 signals across all 12 teams are tag 'default_hold' with the reason string 'Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.', which BuySellHold.jsx renders verbatim as the rationale. movers.roster / movers.league / movers.top150 are [] for all 12 teams, portfolio.biggestRisk / tradeChip / buyLow are null for all 12, and volExposure is 100% 'unknown'. The same payload's delta detail is honest — reason 'low_history_coverage', reliable false, coverageFraction 0.0 — and TeamCommandHeader.jsx renders 'Insufficient rank history for a reliable number.' So one panel says unmeasured and the other asserts stability, from the identical payload.

reproduction.command: ls -la data/rank_history.jsonl ; python3 -c "import json,collections; c=collections.Counter(json.loads(l)['date'] for l in open('data/source_value_history.jsonl')); print(dict(c))" ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/terminal?team=468418790212759552' | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(collections.Counter(s['tag'] for s in d['signals'])); print(d['teamAggregates']['delta7dDetail']['reason'], d['meta']['historyPlayerCount'])"
reproduction.expected: a signal set that distinguishes 'no history' from 'stable'
reproduction.actual: ls: data/rank_history.jsonl: No such file or directory ; source_value_history dates {'2026-08-04': 1} ; Counter({'default_hold': 57}) ; delta reason 'low_history_coverage' ; meta.historyPlayerCount 0

numericProof.formula: share of signals whose rationale asserts stability while trend inputs are null

userImpact: The Signals panel presents 57 confident 'Stable' verdicts per team on a dataset that measured nothing. A manager reads 'no movement' as evidence rather than as absence of evidence.

priorFinding.note: Independently confirmed that terminal.py's buy-low keeps only the short-drop leg (rank<=150, value>=3000, rankChange<=-3) while emitting metric 'short_drop_long_steady' — no 30-day leg exists at src/api/terminal.py:1013-1046. On this snapshot rankChange is 0 for every row so buyLow is null on all 12 teams and the mislabel is currently inert.

whatWorks: The delta path degrades correctly and says so, end to end, from the reason code to the rendered string. That is the pattern the signal path should follow.
rootCause: The 'no rule fired' fallback string was written for a populated-history world and is reused when the inputs are absent.
requiredRepair: Branch the fallback on whether any trend input was measurable and emit a distinct tag (e.g. 'no_history') so the UI can say 'not measured' instead of 'stable'. Container caveat: data/rank_history.jsonl is absent here; the mislabel is a code property, not an artifact of that absence.

title: The gameplan recommendation objects state benefit and confidence but never cost; risk is reported only at position level and horizon only via a field the payload itself marks non-sortable
claimUnderTest: Prompt: do recommendations state benefit, cost, risk, confidence and horizon?
observed: Per-player targets carry BENEFIT (lineupGain, an exact re-solve delta — Travis Etienne +16.11), CONFIDENCE (0.5, and 0.85/0.0 at position level), and a reason plus a named corroborating-signal list. They carry NO COST — the payload states this explicitly in limitations.targets.cannotSupport: 'Any claim about what a trade will COST. The engines rank what is worth wanting, not what it takes to get it.' marketEdge is null on all 74 candidates because market_prices is deliberately omitted (coverage.marketEdgeUnmeasured explains that no validated conversion exists between the 0-100 rosValue index and the 0-9999 dynasty market). RISK appears only as positional concentrationRisk, never per recommendation. HORIZON appears only as targetPositions[].winNowWeight, which fieldPolicy.nonSortable and nonFilterable both disqualify because it carries two different quantities depending on viability. So 2 of 5 requested attributes are present per recommendation.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan?team=468418790212759552' | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);t=[p for p in d['targetPlayers'] if p['recommended']][0];print(sorted(t.keys()));print(t);print(d['limitations']['targets']['cannotSupport'][1])"
reproduction.expected: benefit, cost, risk, confidence, horizon on each recommendation
reproduction.actual: keys = [availability, confidence, corroborating, lineupGain, marketEdge, modelVersion, name, notes, playerId, position, priority, reason, recommended, signals] ; marketEdge null ; no cost field ; cannotSupport names the omission

numericProof.formula: count of {benefit, cost, risk, confidence, horizon} present on a targetPlayers row

userImpact: Zero today (no UI). Recorded because the gap is structural, not a bug: without an acquisition-cost scale the engine can rank what is worth wanting but cannot rank what is worth paying for, and any UI built on it would present a benefit with no price.
whatWorks: This is the most honest omission set in the codebase. Every missing quantity is named, explained, and given a 'whatWouldUnlockMore' entry; the corroboration gate refuses to recommend on our own valuation alone (6 of 74 recommended, and coverage.corroborationYield explains that a yield near 100% would mean a corroborator had been fabricated); acceptancePlausibility carries a neverRenamed policy forbidding the word probability.
rootCause: No acquisition-cost scale exists in the platform, and rosValue (0-100 index) and canonicalSiteValues (0-9999 market) have no validated conversion.
requiredRepair: Supply a rest-of-season-denominated price per player, as coverage.marketEdgeUnmeasured.wouldUnlock specifies.

title: src/ros/direction.py's roster-strength percentile and roster age profile have no effect on any label, and only three of its seven labels occur on live data
claimUnderTest: direction.py module docstring: 'Combines: Playoff odds, Championship odds, Team ROS strength, Roster age profile.' classify_team docstring: 'The spec's ranges overlap intentionally so a team's exact band can shift on age + roster strength.'
observed: classify_team(playoff=0.0, champ=0.0, strength=0.0|0.5|1.0) returns 'Seller' in all three cases — strength_pct is bound at :78 and read only inside the summary f-string. build_section() calls build_team_directions() with no teams=, so team_obj is None, roster_age is {}, age_heavy is always False, and 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' can never fire in production (it does fire when vetCount>=4 is supplied). The in-file comment '_ = snapshot  # roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly' is false — build_roster_age_profile is never called on any production path. Sweeping the full (playoff, championship) grid with an empty age profile reaches 6 of 7 labels; restricting playoff to the two values the sim actually emits (0.0 and 1.0) reaches 4; the live board shows 3 (Strong Buyer, Hold / Evaluate, Seller). frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx additionally defines a LABEL_COLOR map for all seven labels and never renders a label at all.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "from src.ros.direction import classify_team; print([classify_team(playoff_odds_pct=0.0,championship_odds_pct=0.0,team_ros_strength_percentile=s)['label'] for s in (0.0,0.5,1.0)]); print(sorted({classify_team(playoff_odds_pct=po,championship_odds_pct=co/100,team_ros_strength_percentile=0.5,roster_age_profile={})['label'] for po in (0.0,1.0) for co in range(101)}))"
reproduction.expected: strength changes the label; all seven labels reachable
reproduction.actual: ['Seller','Seller','Seller'] ; reachable with binary playoff odds = ['Buyer','Hold / Evaluate','Seller','Strong Buyer']

numericProof.formula: count of distinct labels emitted over the live 12-team board

userImpact: The /league Trade Deadline table renders a STRENGTH column that provably does not influence the DIRECTION column beside it, and the page's own subtitle claims the label is 'based on ROS playoff + championship odds + team strength + roster age' when two of those four do nothing.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced both dead inputs by direct invocation and enumerated label reachability three ways (full grid 6/7, binary-odds 4/7, live 3/7). Extends prior F04, which stated one unreachable label; with the sim emitting only 0.0/1.0 playoff odds, three more are unreachable in practice. The RosTradeFitPanel dead LABEL_COLOR map is also new.

whatWorks: The classifier is deterministic and the summary string honestly reports all three numbers it was given, which is what makes the contradiction in W20-F002 visible on the page.
rootCause: Two of four documented inputs were never wired; the label bands were specified against continuous playoff odds that the simulator does not produce.
requiredRepair: Either wire strength and age into the branches as documented or delete them from the docstring and the page subtitle; and pass teams= from build_section so build_roster_age_profile actually runs.
